name: Sylius
title: Sylius SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Sylius’s shop API: 24 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; wishlist, vendors and CMS pages are gaps. Setup and fixes.
lede: Solid core coverage: cart, checkout and sign-in are wired against Sylius’s shop API. Sylius picks the channel from the request’s host, so the URL you give the connector decides which channel the storefront sells from.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; wishlist, vendors and CMS pages are not.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Sylius channel

quickStartNote: The guide removes only `@misiki/litekart-connector`. A fresh clone’s `package.json` also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector`, and with two connectors installed and neither of them Litekart’s, the build stops and asks for `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR` — so this removes both.

env.name: PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_URL
env.note: Your Sylius URL. Sylius picks the channel from this URL’s host — there is no channel header or parameter. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_SYLIUS_LOCALE_CODE
env.note: Such as `de_DE`, sent as `Accept-Language`. Sylius falls back to the channel’s default locale.

env.name: PUBLIC_SYLIUS_STORE_ID
env.note: Treated as the channel code, and used only to read that channel’s details.

env.name: PUBLIC_SYLIUS_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: Sent as a bearer token when set.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/sylius-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_CHANNEL_ID`, which cannot work against a stock install — the channel comes from the host — and `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_KEY`, `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_SECRET` and `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_ACCESS_KEY`, which the connector’s source does not read.
backendSettings: Point `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_URL` at the hostname of the channel you want to sell from: Sylius resolves the channel from the request’s host.
Let the storefront’s origin make cross-origin requests to Sylius (CORS): in production the browser calls `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_URL` directly, not only the server.
howItWorks: The connector speaks Sylius’s shop API. The channel is whichever one Sylius matches to the host of `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_URL`; the locale travels as `Accept-Language`. The API documentation URL its authors were given was dead, so it was written from Sylius’s own source instead.

Installing the package is the whole switch. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever `@misiki/*-connector` is installed, and `src/lib/core/connectors/init.ts` hands it every `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_*` variable that is set, camel-cased, at boot — in the server hook for server rendering and in the client hook for the browser, which must reach the same URL in production.

There is no Litekart API behind the storefront here, so store identity — name, logo, currency, menus, plugin toggles, theme colours — comes from `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` merged under the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`. Until you override it, the store is called “Test”. Any Litekart REST path the connector still inherits is answered from that local data, or resolved empty, rather than requested.
limitations: CMS pages: not wired — legal and CMS pages render their layout with empty content.
Pages that depend on a service that is not wired render their empty state rather than failing.
Homepage sections other than the live product list come from the active theme’s static content — the standing rule for themes.
The Conversational Shopping assistant is Litekart-only; its widget stays hidden when another connector is active.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the sylius connector is active but PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/sylius-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “PUBLIC_…_API_URL is set, but it configures a different backend than the one this build runs on”
troubleshooting.fix: Another backend’s variable is still set, usually left over from the one you switched from. Remove it, or install that backend’s connector. `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL` is exempt: it only points the dev proxy.

troubleshooting.problem: The store is called “Test”, or shows the wrong name and logo
troubleshooting.fix: Store identity is static on this backend. Set `name`, `logo`, `currencyCode` and the rest in the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`; `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` lists every field.

troubleshooting.problem: `[sylius] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if Sylius has no such feature; if it has one, the fix belongs in the connector’s matching service.

troubleshooting.problem: `http proxy error: api/... ECONNREFUSED` in dev
troubleshooting.fix: A Litekart REST path was requested from outside the connector, so its guard never saw it. Vite proxies `/api` to `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL`, or to `localhost:7000`.

`@misiki/kitcommerce-core` declares it as a peer, and `vite.config.ts` redirects that specifier to whichever connector is installed. Make sure exactly one `@misiki/*-connector` is listed in `package.json`.

faq.q: Can I run a Sylius store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; wishlist, vendors and CMS pages are not. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production Sylius store.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Sylius?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/sylius-connector`, set `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: How does Svelte Commerce pick a Sylius channel?
faq.a: By host. Sylius resolves the channel from the host of the request, so point `PUBLIC_SYLIUS_API_URL` at the channel’s hostname. There is no channel header or parameter to set instead.

faq.q: Has the Sylius connector been run against a real Sylius store?
faq.a: Not against a live production instance — no Svelte Commerce connector has been. It was written by reading Sylius’s authoritative API source, and the Svelte Commerce maintainers ask Sylius’s own maintainers for a sandbox to run it against.
